description: Key chain connector - one at each end of each key board's flat flex ribbon, on the main board and on the key board
notes: Quantity is the tracked figure chain-connectors; do not restate it. PINOUT, NUMBERED AT THE MAIN-BOARD END: 1 GND, 2 SCK, 3 GND, 4 SH/LD, 5 GND, 6 SER, 7 GND, 8 QH, 9 GND, 10 3V3, 11 spare, 12 spare - a ground between every signal (ADR 0001 item 1). Conductor 6 is the key board's own serial input and conductor 8 its own serial output, on both ribbons, so both key boards are wired alike. THE SAME PART AT ALL FOUR POSITIONS, side-entry, the ribbon entering from the side-wall side at both ends (mechanical/DESIGN.md). *** THE KEY BOARD'S PIN NUMBERS ARE MIRRORED: conductor k is main-board pin k and key-board pin 13-k. *** The key board's connector is the same part turned upside down with the same entry side, and that reverses its row. KEY-BOARD PINOUT: 11 SCK, 9 SH/LD, 7 SER, 5 QH, 3 3V3, 12/10/8/6/4 GND, 2 and 1 spare. Net the key board's J-CHAIN by 13-k; place the standard footprint on the bottom side (do not hand-mirror it - that would reverse it twice) [calc, key-chain-loom.md; confirm against the chosen part's pin-1 drawing]. Same part both ends is also what makes the cable same-side contact (FFC-CHAIN). Envelope: config/body.yaml boards.ffc_conn_l/w/h, all tbd [from memory]. OPEN, DECIDED AT M4 WITH THE PART: the part number; top- or bottom-contact (either, if all four are the same); a height inside boards.ffc_conn_h; and an FFC thickness at the contacts that matches FFC-CHAIN

part: 12-way 1.0mm pitch flat flex cable, same-side contacts
description: Key chain ribbon - one per key board, main board to key board, in one 180-degree C
notes: One per key board (PCB-CLUSTER): the key chain's only conductors off the main board. Conductor order is J-CHAIN's. *** SAME-SIDE CONTACTS (both ends exposed on the same face). *** J-CHAIN is the same part at both ends and the C turns the ribbon over, so the face that meets the main board's contacts is the face that meets the key board's [calc, key-chain-loom.md]. An opposite-side cable works only with one top-contact and one bottom-contact connector - two parts to stock for nothing. Width and thickness: config/body.yaml routing.ffc_w and routing.ffc_t, tbd [from memory]; the thickness at the contacts is whatever J-CHAIN's datasheet specifies. LENGTH OPEN, DECIDED AT M4: mechanical/drc.echo 'ribbon arc length' (the arc with its slack) plus the two insertion depths off J-CHAIN's drawing, rounded up to a stock length

description: Series damping at the chain driving end on SCK, SH/LD and the chain-end SER
notes: On the main board where the MCU's pins arrive, before anything else on the net. SCK and SH/LD each reach four 74HC165s: right_thumb and left_thumb on the main board, and one at the far end of each key board's ribbon, over up to the main board's length (mechanical/drc.echo 'main board (derived)'). At that length an MCU edge sees a line rather than a lump [calc, key-chain-loom.md]. Edge-rate damping at the source - NOT series termination, which ADR 0001 rejected (as R-TERM-CHAIN) for a line that drops on four registers. Same 100R as R-SPI-SER. OPEN, DECIDED AT E14: scope SCK at the left_hand register on the real main board and ribbons; fit if it rings through the 74HC165 thresholds. Three 0805s either way

description: ESD protection on the MCU pins the key chain brings to the main board's ribbon connectors
notes: FIT IT (ADR 0018). Channels: SCK, SH/LD and the chain-end SER (IO38, IO7, IO33, each on the connector side of its R-CHAIN-SER); the fourth is spare. The chain's QH into the MCU (IO40) comes from right_thumb on the main board and reaches no connector. Return to GND_CHAIN, the main board's ground pour. WHY: with the lid off and a ZIF latch open, a main-board J-CHAIN exposes three MCU pins behind 100R to a hand - and the ribbons are re-seated every time the lid goes back on. It cannot be added once the board is made, and it costs pennies. PLACE IT at the left_hand J-CHAIN, which carries all three channels; SCK and SH/LD reach the right_hand J-CHAIN on the same nets. PACKAGE: SP0504BAHTG is SOT23-5 with 4 CH per the banked SP0504BAHT.pdf p.1 ordering table; SOT23-6 is SP0505BAHTG with 5 CH. All channels share one common pin. It and U-TVS-SPI are two packages because each clamps at its own connector, and J-UMB and the J-CHAIN are at different places on the main board

part: Ferrite bead 600R @ 100MHz or more, DCR 0.1R or less, rated 0.5A or more
description: Series isolation on the 3V3 conductor of each key board's ribbon, on the main board
notes: ONE PER RIBBON, in series between the main board's 3V3 (DEV_3V3 - the Matrix's ME6217C33M5G LDO, reaching the main board on CBL-MCU-RIBBON) and that ribbon's conductor 10 (main-board J-CHAIN pin 10). right_thumb, left_thumb and R-SER-TERM stay on DEV_3V3 directly. IT IS ISOLATION, NOT PROTECTION: it keeps a key board's register edges off the rail that is also the MCP3202's reference. SHORT-CIRCUIT PROTECTION IS THE LDO'S OWN (ADR 0018): datasheets/discrete-and-power/ME6217C33M5G.pdf p.1 'a built-in overcurrent protector' and thermal shutdown at 160C; p.4 Ishort 350mA TYPICAL at VOUT = 0V, with no min or max. The short to expect is a ribbon seated skewed across main-board J-CHAIN pins 9/10 at reassembly: the whole 3V3 rail collapses, the Matrix does not start, and it is seen on the bench before the lid is closed. VERIFY AT E1: short one ribbon's 3V3 to GND through 1 ohm at J-CHAIN, confirm the rail limits and the Matrix restarts when it is removed. RATINGS: rated current at or above 0.5A, because the bead carries the LDO's limit (350mA typ) for as long as a short lasts [calc]. DCR 0.1R or less: at the chain's whole 27.3mA (19 closed keys at 1.43mA) that is 2.7mV at most [calc]. CHECK AT E14: the bead and the key board's C-DECOUPLE-165 (100nF) form an LC near 0.5MHz if the bead is ~1uH below its resistive band [calc, bead inductance from memory], close to the chain's clock; scope the key board's VCC while shifting and add a damping bulk cap on the key board if it rings. PART NUMBER OPEN [from memory: 0805 beads meeting all three figures are a stock family]

description: Pull-up on the chain-end serial input, on the main board
notes: left_hand's SER, which leaves on conductor 6 of its ribbon (main-board J-CHAIN pin 6, key-board pin 7). ON THE MAIN BOARD at that ribbon's J-CHAIN, on the connector side of R-CHAIN-SER - so the two key boards stay identical. Holds the chain-end input high when nothing drives it, which is the tied-off case ADR 0001 specified. If firmware DRIVES it from IO33, the 100R series wins against 10k to within 33mV of the rail (3.3V x 100/10100) - so an end-to-end self-test (shift a known pattern through all 32 bits, and through both ribbons in both directions) is a FIRMWARE choice rather than a board choice. Fit it. Whether firmware uses it is decided at E4
